name: Lawn care business
blurb: Mow, edge and tidy lawns for regular clients, usually on a weekly or fortnightly route
title: Lawn Care Business: How to Start, Costs and Risks
description: How a lawn care or lawn mowing business makes money, the equipment you need, who it suits, the seasonal and safety risks, and how to test it locally.
h1: How to start a lawn care business
answer: A lawn care business mows, edges and tidies gardens for homeowners and businesses, usually on a repeating weekly or fortnightly route, and can add services like hedge trimming, leaf clearing and seasonal clean-ups. You can start with a mower, a trimmer and a vehicle. The catches are seasonality, weather, equipment wear and the fact that your route, not your price, decides most of your profit.

sections.h: How a lawn care business makes money
body: Most clients pay per visit or a set monthly amount for regular mowing during the growing season. Extras such as hedge cutting, leaf removal, aeration, planting or garden clean-ups raise the value of each visit.
What eats the margin is driving time, fuel, equipment repairs, insurance and rain days. Clients close together on one route earn far more per hour than the same number spread across town.

ul: A reliable mower, a string trimmer or edger, a blower and safety gear such as eye and ear protection.
A vehicle and possibly a trailer, plus a way to dispose of grass and green waste.
Liability insurance: stones thrown by a mower can break windows or hurt people.

Local paperwork: rules differ by country and city. You may need a business licence, and chemical treatments can need a licence of their own; for example in the US, restricted-use pesticides may only be applied by a certified applicator or under one's direct supervision.
A simple schedule and invoicing app so routes and payments stay organised.

sections.h: Who it suits (and who it doesn't)

head: Suits
Not for
rows: People who enjoy outdoor, physical work
Anyone who needs the same income every month
Someone handy with engines and small repairs
People with hay fever or back problems
Students or part-timers with free days in the growing season
Places with a very short growing season and no winter work

ul: Seasonality: in many climates mowing stops in winter. Plan winter work such as leaf clearing, snow removal or other services, or save from summer.
Weather: rain pushes jobs back and squeezes your week.
Underpricing: low prices win clients quickly but leave nothing for equipment replacement.
Injury and damage: mowers and trimmers cause real injuries, and thrown stones break glass and cars.
Chemicals: offering weed or pest treatments without the right licence can break the law in many places.

sections.h: How to test it cheaply first

ol: Look at maps and local groups to see how many lawn care services cover your area.
Mow three lawns for neighbours at a real price and time each visit including travel.
Ask whether they would book every week or fortnight and what they would pay.
Put a simple flyer through doors on one street and count calls.
Calculate what a full route of clients close together would earn after fuel and wear.
Register the business, get liability insurance and check any licence you need.
Buy dependable used or entry-level equipment and keep spare blades and line.
Focus marketing on a few neighbourhoods so your route stays tight.
Offer a recurring plan with a set price and clear rules for rain days and skipped visits.
Keep a log of time, fuel and repairs per client and drop the ones that do not pay.

faq.q: Is a lawn mowing business a good side hustle?
faq.a: It can be, because jobs are short and many clients are flexible on timing. It works best when you can cover a few neighbourhoods in one or two days and accept that winter will be quiet.

faq.q: Do I need a licence for a lawn care business?
faq.a: It depends on where you are. Many places require a general business licence, and applying pesticides or herbicides commonly needs separate certification. Check with your local authority before offering treatments.

faq.q: How do I get my first lawn care clients?
faq.a: Neighbours, door flyers, local community groups and map listings work well because clients want someone nearby. Ask every early client for a review and a referral to their neighbours.
